title: Locks and concurrent changes
goal: Protect a balance check against concurrent changes and reproduce two-transaction ordering.
prerequisites: onec.p9; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.
outcomes: Show how two individually valid decisions produce−4.
Actual input/output and exact own source identified; unperformed stages marked NOT RUN.
Accepted original preserved; rejection and its limits explained.
sections: Two operations each read balance 10 and spend 7. Each passes alone; combined balance−4 breaks the rule. A post-read check without coordinated locking does not prevent the second transaction. Starting a transaction alone does not specify lock scope. Draw read A → readB → write A → write B before choosing an API.

The runnable local experiment creates own 30/45 documents. A transaction locks Document.ЗаявкаУслуги by the first reference, writes 99 and rolls back. Expect 30 and the untouched 45. This proves actual lock API/rollback, not a two-session race.

Managed locking identifies a data space and dimension values. Lock invariant-related data before deciding. Too-wide locks reduce concurrency; too-narrow locks miss conflicts. Scope depends on register, mode and operation; there is no universal line suitable for every solution.

Lock scope follows the invariant. A shared customer/period resource may need a broader key than one document reference. Define competing read/check/write operations first. Locking the entire infobase merely to avoid errors is not a justified design.

Two operations locking A/Bin opposite order can deadlock. Agree on stable-key order and keep transactions short. A timeout is failure, not a successful spend. Retrying needs idempotency and a fresh state read; blindly repeating external effects can duplicate them.

Draw a separate schedule: both actors read 10 and request 7. Correct serialization makes the second reread 3 and reject. A real test needs two permitted concurrent sessions with controlled pauses; a single-user training installation does not prove it.

Single-sessiontrainingcannot prove this scenario. In a permitted multi-session stand, control barriers and record both traces and final balance. From 10, one spend 7 succeeds; the second rereads and rejects, result 3. Test an independent customer to show the lock does not block everything.

In another copy replace rollback with commit:99 persists and the 30 assertion fails. Retain the failed protocol and corrected source. Timeouts, deadlocks and a server cluster remain separate scenarios until actually tested.
